factsfirstdaily.subject: Anthropic's IPO Week Tests the AI Industry
factsfirstdaily.preview_text: A senator presses Lutnick on chips, Gaza tents wait at the border and Voyager 1 nears a milestone.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO Week Becomes a Test for the Whole AI Industry

photo.alt: The Nasdaq tower display in Times Square, New York; file photo.

paragraphs: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, is expected to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday. CNBC reports the offering matters to almost every major tech company. Shares are expected to price at $70 to $78.
The offering could raise over $90 billion. CNBC reports the company is eyeing a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion. It already holds $132 billion in cash, including short-term investments.

Seven chip and cloud giants, including Nvidia, Google and Microsoft, are buying $26 billion of stock at the IPO price. Anthropic lists over $900 billion in spending commitments in its prospectus. It posted a net loss of $104 billion through nine months.

Why it matters. The sale could show whether investors will keep funding the costly AI buildout. CNBC reports traders are also awaiting Nvidia's earnings after the bell on Tuesday. Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.79% on CNBC's live page at about 6:07 a.m. ET Monday.

stories.title: Senator Cantwell Presses Lutnick to Stop AI Chip Sales to China

photo.alt: A silicon wafer of computer chips; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: Sen. Maria Cantwell sent Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick a letter on Sunday about AI chip exports. CNBC reports she alleged his department failed to stop China from getting the most advanced U.S. chips.

Cantwell is the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee. She urged Lutnick to enforce a 2018 export control law. She also cited a 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China. She said it could create a perverse incentive to approve exports.

The pressure follows Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia chief. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a dramatic shakeup at Nvidia on Sunday. He questioned whether the company pursued illicit chip sales to lift earnings.

Why it matters. Export controls are meant to protect America's lead in artificial intelligence. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate banking committee in December. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CNBC on Monday.

stories.title: Four Allies Urge Israel to Let 150,000 Tents Into Gaza Before Winter

photo.alt: Tents and laundry in a displacement camp; illustrative file photo, not Gaza.

paragraphs: The foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom issued a joint appeal on Sunday. They said 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at Gaza's border.

The ministers urged Israel to stop the delays and allow rapid, unimpeded aid access. They said the crossings must be opened and the tents allowed in. They also asked for entry of dual-use items needed for recovery.

Heavy rain this month swept away tens of thousands of tents in Gaza. Al Jazeera reports more than 1.9 million people are displaced, according to the United Nations. A shelter group estimated residents need at least 121,000 tents.

Why it matters. Winter is setting in for families with little protection from cold and rain. The European Union and a UN team issued similar warnings in recent days. The ministers said there is still time to act.

stories.title: Voyager 1 Is About to Become the First Craft One Light-Day From Earth

photo.alt: A large radio antenna dish under a night sky; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: NASA's Voyager 1 is set to reach a new milestone on Wednesday. ABC News reports it will be one light-day from Earth at 5:16 a.m. ET. It will be the first human-made object that far away.
A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, more than 16 billion miles. The probe is traveling at about 38,000 mph. It launched in 1977 on what was meant to be a five-year mission.
Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn and found a faint ring system around Jupiter. NPR reports NASA is asking the public to flash the probe's call sign, VGR, in Morse code on Tuesday night.

Why it matters. The aging probe still sends data from interstellar space nearly 50 years after launch. Voyager 1 and its twin are the only spacecraft to have operated outside the heliosphere. That bubble shields the solar system.

deep_dive.title: What Yemen's Retreat From the Bab Al-Mandab Means for Shipping

photo.alt: A cargo ship sails on open water; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces have pulled back from ground overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key maritime choke point. BBC News reports the redeployment would reinforce Aden. Houthi-run media say the group has taken control of the evacuated territory. The Houthis seized ground near the strait in a surprise offensive in September. Government forces launched a campaign in October to take it back. The withdrawal ends that weeks-long offensive.

Reuters says the retreat gives the Houthis greater leverage over a key maritime choke point. Saudi Arabia has relied on Red Sea routes for oil exports since the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. Iran is still disrupting traffic through Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.

The Southern Armed Forces said on Sunday that troops were leaving Dhubab Airport and the strait area. NBC News, carrying a Reuters report, says they are redeploying toward Aden, where the government is based. The Houthis say they pose no threat to international shipping.

The government says securing Aden is now its priority. The Houthis say they will keep targeting Saudi vessels. They have repeatedly attacked Aden in recent weeks. The UN estimates nearly 330,000 people have been displaced as fighting escalated.

trivia.question: In what year did NASA launch Voyager 1?
trivia.explanation: B. 1977. NPR reports the probe launched on Sept. 5, 1977.

Banks reshape jobs around AI. Barclays plans 5,000 job cuts in 2026 as lenders automate routine work; CNBC reports.
The score: 49ers and Bills stay on top. Both share the NFL's best record at 8-1 after week 10, while the Chiefs and Bengals moved to 7-2; BBC Sport reports.
McIlroy takes the Race to Dubai. Rory McIlroy won his eighth title, matching Colin Montgomerie's record, as Tyrell Hatton won the finale; BBC Sport reports.

A year of free childcare. New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every family regardless of income; NPR reports.

stories.title: A Fed Official Says Inflation Is Moving in the Wrong Direction

photo.alt: Shopper pushing a grocery cart; file photo, 2023.

paragraphs: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said Sunday the central bank has some work to do on inflation. CNBC reports he said price pressures are running too hot, with inflation uncomfortably above the 2% target. He did not specifically call for more rate hikes.

CNBC reported Sunday that futures markets fully priced a quarter-point hike in December. Reuters reports Tuesday's retail sales report will show how shoppers are coping with higher gasoline prices and borrowing costs. Walmart, Target, Home Depot and Lowe's also report results. Before the open, CNBC's live page showed S&P 500 futures down 0.25% at about 6:07 a.m. ET Monday.

stories.title: A Vulcan Rocket Fails After Liftoff and Destroys 40 Amazon Satellites

photo.alt: Rocket climbing through clouds; file photo, 2026.

paragraphs: Reuters reports a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral on Sunday. It destroyed 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network. It was the launch company's first mission failure.

ULA is a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin. The cause was not immediately clear, Reuters reports. The loss is a major setback for Vulcan, the company's new flagship rocket, as it sought a regular launch pace for Amazon.

stories.title: Estonia Will Close Its Border Crossings With Russia After a Suspected Arson Attempt

photo.alt: Old Town skyline of Tallinn, Estonia; file photo, 2026.

paragraphs: Reuters reports Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from Dec. 1. Authorities detained eight people over a suspected attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems. Officials said Russia's GRU military intelligence ordered it.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said the closures send a clear message to the Kremlin. He said Russia's hostile actions come at a cost. He plans to press for tougher sanctions and a stricter visa policy at Monday's EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels.

stories.title: Huge Crowds Rally in Prague Against a Plan to Change Public Media Funding

photo.alt: Crowds on Charles Bridge in Prague; file photo, 2025.

paragraphs: Reuters reports hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against a government media funding plan. It would cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget. Critics say that would dent broadcasters' independence.

Al Jazeera reports the current monthly household fee is 205 crowns, about $9.45. Prime Minister Andrej Babis's government says editorial independence will not be affected. The bill passed a preliminary vote and awaits further debate. The rally came days before the Nov. 17 holiday marking the Velvet Revolution.

deep_dive.title: Why Congo's Ebola Outbreak Is Still Out of Control After Six Months

photo.alt: Lab worker holding a sample plate; file photo, 2021.

paragraphs: What happened. Reuters reports Africa CDC says the Ebola outbreak in Congo is still out of control six months after it was declared. Director-general Jean Kaseya cited deadly attacks on health workers, unpaid staff and a lack of resources. More than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been recorded since May 15.

Why it matters. Al Jazeera reports it is the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record. Cases have been reported in East, Central and West Africa, the widest spread on the continent yet. No vaccine or treatment exists specifically for the Bundibugyo strain. It kills about half of the people it infects.

What each side says. Kaseya said more than 80% of new cases emerge outside contact lists. He called coordination between Congo and donors a collective failure, though he said he was not pointing fingers. Only $1.3 billion of the $2.9 billion pledged by donors has been released, Al Jazeera reports.

What comes next. The World Health Organization approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines earlier this month and expects results in early 2027. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said transmission is slowing in several early epicentres. At least 3,000 people have recovered and returned home, Al Jazeera reports.

World view: Cape Verde votes for a president. Incumbent Jose Maria Neves faced the archipelago's first female candidate in a vote focused on jobs for young people; Reuters reports.
Jordan sentences three to death. A security court convicted the men over a church attack in Karak last month that killed nine people; Reuters reports.
Manila and Canberra sign a defence pact. The arrangement is meant to lower hurdles to joint military activities as security ties deepen; Reuters reports.
The Canary Islands see the most arrivals in a day since 2020. Spain's maritime rescue service saved 1,488 migrants in 14 boats on Saturday; Reuters reports, citing EFE.

Trump's judge push meets resistance. Some Republicans are balking at confirming more judges before Democrats take control of the Senate; Reuters reports.
Young men swung to Democrats. An estimated 59% of men ages 18 to 29 backed Democratic House candidates, a Tufts center found; Reuters reports.
Rubio attacks the ICC. His first prepared speech since the midterms fueled talk about whether he will run for president in 2028; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Japan's economy unexpectedly shrinks. The Nikkei 225 fell 2.42% Monday after third-quarter GDP data, and South Korea's Kospi slumped 3.59%; CNBC reports.
UniCredit wins EU approval for Commerzbank. The European Commission cleared the Italian lender's takeover of its German peer on Monday; CNBC reports.
J&J could announce a deal worth up to $3.4 billion. Johnson & Johnson could announce a purchase of Texas-based Ollin Biosciences as soon as Monday, the FT said; Reuters reports.
SpaceX trades just above its IPO price. The stock last traded near $139 against its $135 offering price, after falling to about $105 in August; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: The FDA rejects a lung cancer drug. Regulators declined Summit Therapeutics' ivonescimab after a trial showed no significant gain in overall survival; Reuters reports.
Apple launches an AI health study. Apple aims to enroll up to 200,000 eligible US iPhone users to ask health questions answered with clinical sources; TechCrunch reports.
Pony.ai turns to domestic chips as supply runs short. Pony.ai's finance chief said the company is turning more to domestically produced chips as demand outstrips supply; TechCrunch reports.
Anthropic's IPO carries huge commitments. The Claude maker has more than $900 billion in spending commitments ahead of its expected Nasdaq debut Thursday; CNBC reports.
The score: Andreeva wins the WTA Finals. The Russian teenager beat Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 without dropping a set; Reuters reports.
England ends Spain's unbeaten run. England won 3-2 in Madrid to top its Nations League group, while Italy crashed out; Reuters reports.
Detroit routs New England in Munich. The Lions won 35-10, and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was injured; Reuters reports.
Arkansas is fined $500,000. The SEC penalized the school after fans stormed the field following a 34-6 upset of South Carolina; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: BTS and Chris Pratt win at the Kids' Choice Awards. Spider-Man: Brand New Day took favorite movie at Nickelodeon's show on Saturday; Reuters reports.
Pope Leo condemns Amazon deforestation. Speaking in the Peruvian Amazon, he also called killings of tribal leaders murders that must be solved; Reuters reports.
Prince Harry visits wounded soldiers in Ukraine. He pledged to bring his Invictus Games to the country once there is peace; Reuters reports.
A notorious cartel founder dies at 80. Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, founder of the Guadalajara cartel, died in hospital on Sunday; Reuters reports.

stories.title: Estonia Will Close Its Russia Border Crossings After a Suspected Attack on a Drone Maker
paragraphs: Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1. The Guardian reports the move follows a suspected sabotage attack on drone maker Threod Systems. Eight people were detained after the attempt on Saturday. Authorities said Russia's GRU military intelligence service ordered it. No injuries or damage were reported.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal linked the attack to Estonia's support for Ukraine. CNBC reports Estonia shares a 294-kilometer border with Russia. Officials said closing the crossings would limit hostile activity and sanctions circumvention. Russia's foreign ministry said it would assess the plans. It called them another bout of Russophobia.

photo.alt: Tallinn old town in Estonia, 2019 file photo

stories.title: Britain Heads Into an EU Summit Promising a Brexit Reset
paragraphs: Prime Minister Andy Burnham hopes to agree a deal with the European Union at a summit on Friday. EU relations minister Hamish Falconer told the BBC the UK would have a voice but no vote on EU food rules. He said the deal could include an exit clause. It would involve no upfront payments.

The Guardian reports Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit has not worked. He says agreements on food, emissions trading and youth mobility could raise GDP by 0.4%. That is about 17 billion pounds. The Conservatives and Reform have said they would undo the reset if they took power.

photo.alt: European Union flags in Brussels, 2020 file photo

stories.title: Australian MP Helen Haines Leaves Hospital Four Weeks After an Alleged Car Attack
paragraphs: Independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital. The BBC reports she was allegedly struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta on Oct. 19. She lost both legs. A 43-year-old man has been charged with offences including causing harm to a public official. He has yet to enter pleas.

The Guardian reports her rehabilitation will continue in Melbourne. Haines said she was full of gratitude for her care. More than 1.46 million Australian dollars has been raised for Save the Children in her name. Police say a motive has not been established. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said his thoughts were with her.

photo.alt: Parliament House flagpole, Canberra, 2022 file photo

deep_dive.title: Asia's Two Biggest Economies Stumble as the IMF Warns About AI
paragraphs: CNBC reports that Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank at an annualized 0.1% in the third quarter. A Reuters poll of economists had expected 0.3% growth. Higher energy import costs cut 0.6 percentage point from growth. Energy subsidies for households reportedly expired in September, exposing consumers to prices pushed up by the Iran war.

China's October data also missed forecasts, CNBC reports. Retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier, against expectations of 0.8%. Industrial output grew 4.8%, below the 5.3% analysts expected. Fixed-asset investment shrank 8.1% in the first ten months. The property downturn has eroded household wealth for a fifth year.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told CNBC the world economy is standing on one leg, artificial intelligence. She warned a wobble could cause financial stability troubles. The IMF estimates circular financing among AI companies at a little over $1 trillion. About two-thirds of it is funded by debt. She spoke at the Asean summit in the Philippines.

The weak Japanese data could complicate the Bank of Japan's plans, CNBC reports. CNBC's early-Monday report put the chance of a December rate rise at 75.6%, citing LSEG. One economist said real final sales fell 2.1% annualized. That is the largest decline outside the pandemic and early 2022. Another economist still expects the central bank to tighten policy.

trivia.question: How many paintings does the 16th-century Book of Miracles contain?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 167. The Guardian reports the manuscript holds 167 paintings of apocalyptic visions and strange weather.
